title: Minimal-actuation feather star–inspired soft swimmers for multimodal 3D maneuverability
abstract: Complex, three-dimensional (3D) motions typically require actuator arrays and complex control architectures. Here, we present a feather star–inspired soft robotic swimmer that uses only two pneumatic inputs to produce three distinct and switchable swimming modes: jellyfish-like pulsation, fishlike propulsion, and rotor-like reorientation. The robot owes this ability to mechanical intelligence: It leverages a monostable instability in its flexible arms to convert two control actuation inputs into 3D swimming modes, including ascension and descension, forward and backward swimming, hovering, and rotation. The robot achieves a maximum swimming speed of 1.64 body lengths per second, minimum cost of transport of 17.6, and peak rotation speed of 90° per second. Particle image velocimetry analyses and computational fluid dynamics simulations reveal distinct vortex structures governing thrust generation and/or rotational torque in each swimming mode. The robot’s minimal input yet multimodal output demonstrates how mechanical intelligence can enable adaptive and multifunctional, yet simple and energy-efficient, robotic and biological swimming mechanisms.

title: Blood Metabolomic Signatures of 1-Hour Glucose Predict Cardiometabolic Risk
abstract: BACKGROUND: Elevated 1-hour glucose levels during an oral glucose tolerance test strongly predict type 2 diabetes (T2D) and cardiovascular disease. We investigated whether the fasting blood metabolome predicting 1-hour glucose could be a target for improving β-cell function, long-term glycemic trajectories, and reducing the risks of T2D and coronary heart disease. We also investigated whether plasma microRNAs derived from key metabolic organs regulate changes in a metabolomic risk score (MRS) for predicting 1-hour glucose. METHODS: Untargeted blood metabolomics and a frequently sampled 75-g oral glucose tolerance test were performed in participants from the OmniCarb trial (n=162). In an independent weight-loss dietary intervention trial (POUNDS Lost [Preventing Overweight Using Novel Dietary Strategies]), temporal changes in MRS and plasma microRNAs measured by genome-wide sequencing were analyzed. In addition, associations of MRS at baseline and its 10-year changes with long-term risk of incident T2D and coronary heart disease were prospectively investigated in the NHS (Nurses’ Health Study). RESULTS: We created a fasting blood MRS for predicting 1-hour glucose (Pearson r =0.8) and found significant associations with half-day (diurnal) postprandial glucose excursions and insulin secretion after 5-week controlled feeding interventions varying in carbohydrate amount and glycemic index. In the POUNDS Lost trial, diet-induced changes in MRSs were related to 2-year trajectories of glucose metabolism; circulating microRNAs regulating cardiometabolic abnormalities were pivotal factors influencing these changes. In the NHS, women in the top 20% of MRS had a multivariate-adjusted relative risk of 3.80 (95% CI, 2.22–6.51) for T2D and 1.48 (95% CI, 1.04–2.12) for coronary heart disease compared with those in the lowest 20%. In addition, 10-year increases in plasma metabolites related to 1-hour glucose were linearly associated with a higher risk of T2D. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that fasting blood metabolomic signatures predicting elevated 1-hour glucose reflect disease pathophysiology and could be targets for preventing T2D and coronary heart disease.

title: pH-responsive manganese carboxymethyl chitosan hydrogel releases pesticide to promote rice tillering and suppress root-parasitic weeds
abstract: Abstract Strigolactone (SL) signaling is an important agricultural target for controlling plant branching and parasitic weeds. Here, based on the SL inhibitor KK094, we describe the design of 32 indole derivatives, of which DK6 exhibits optimal activity. To enhance solubility and bioavailability, we describe a pH-responsive manganese-coordinated carboxymethyl chitosan hydrogel (CMCS-DK6), showing sustained release under alkaline conditions. We demonstrate CMCS-DK6 strongly inhibits germination of parasitic weeds, especially Striga asiatica (IC 50 = 1.80 μM), while promoting rice tillering, reducing height, and increasing dry weight. Molecular simulations, along with microscale thermophoresis results, suggest that DK6 binds stably to SL receptors. Transcriptomics reveal DK6 suppresses SL signaling, modulates metabolic pathways, and interacts with hormone pathways to regulate tillering. This work offers a hydrogel delivery strategy and some potential mechanistic implications for improving crop architecture and weed control.

title: Urban Vernacular Transitions: Contesting Commercial Space Through Everyday Practices in Bangkok’s Privately-Owned Public Spaces
journal: Journal of Architectural/Planning Research and Studies (JARS)
abstract: This paper explores the transition of vernacular architecture from rural traditions to urban adaptations,expanding the discussion toward what may be termed the “urban vernacular.” While rural vernacular has longbeen associated with natural materials, collective labour, and the continuity of cultural wisdom, the urbanvernacular emerges in contexts marked by industrialised construction, consumer culture, and the negotiationof everyday life in rapidly growing cities. Privately-Owned Public Spaces (POPS) in Bangkok are introducedas illustrative cases through which these dynamics can be observed. Although designed as commercial interiors,malls and their semi-public areas are tactically re-appropriated by diverse groups: students transform foodcourts into study zones, elderly visitors establish routines of repeated occupation, and youth communitiesadapt mirrored walls for dance practice. Such activities reveal how POPS, despite their regulated and privatelymanaged frameworks, provide informal third places that foster social interaction, comfort, and adaptability. Thestudy employed non-participant observation and photographic documentation across selected malls, focusingon patterns of use that extend beyond consumption. These observations highlight how POPS serve as a lensto interpret broader processes of vernacular transition. The paper argues that urban vernacular heritage liesless in the preservation of form than in the recognition of lived practices that sustain cultural meaning. Byframing POPS as an example rather than an endpoint, the research underscores the resilience of improvisation,collectivity, and cultural continuity within contemporary urban conditions. While these spaces demonstratevernacular resilience through everyday improvisation, the analysis also exposes their precarity, a conditionshaped by surveillance, selective tolerance, and corporate governance that renders user autonomy contingentand unstable. This tension between resilience and precarity defines the contested terrain of urban vernacularpractices within Bangkok’s privately-owned public spaces.

title: Understanding out-of-home food waste among young Chinese adults: a photo-elicitation study
abstract: Purpose This research examines how young Chinese adults understand and negotiate responsibility for food waste when dining out at the intersection of multiple cultural values. Design/methodology/approach This paper reports on a qualitative photo-elicitation study in which 20 young adults from China were asked to take photos when dining out. Follow-up interviews were conducted to explore the story behind photos. Data were analysed using an adaptive theory approach coupled with a moral economy lens to examine how cultural norms shape action. Findings Young Chinese adults' understandings and negotiation of responsibility for out-of-home food waste are embedded within intersecting normative narratives including relational harmony, market entitlement and personal standards. The data demonstrates that, even when moral concerns against food waste exist, responsibility is negotiated across social relationships. Market-based logic further legitimises this redistribution through economic values and market exchange. Together, these intersecting norms create a situation in which responsibility is negotiated and distributed rather than individually assumed. Originality/value This study spotlights a moral-economic “responsibilisation” dilemma faced by young Chinese adults from a cultural-normative perspective and highlights the need to develop new food waste avoidance norms grounded in existing and dominant Chinese cultural norms.

title: Towards a suitable biomarker for childhood screening for familial hypercholesterolemia: a systematic literature review
abstract: Abstract Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is a common genetic disorder causing elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c) concentrations from birth, resulting in a high risk of premature cardiovascular disease. Despite effective early treatment, FH remains underdiagnosed in children, highlighting the need for universal screening. This systematic review aims to evaluate the available evidence regarding suitable biomarkers for the purpose of universal screening for FH in childhood. The electronic databases Medline and Embase were systematically searched for studies comparing blood biomarkers in children with heterozygous FH and non-FH children. Of the 2,488 studies found, 35 were included. Although the data were constrained by considerable heterogeneity, LDL-c, total cholesterol (TC), and apolipoprotein B (ApoB) concentrations were consistently higher in children with FH across the included studies. Furthermore, increased non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-c), lathosterol, sitosterol and TC/HDL-c ratio, and a decreased squalene/TC ratio were found in children with FH. Only three screening studies combined biomarker (LDL-c, non-HDL-c and TC) and genetic testing simultaneously, revealing however limited sensitivity and specificity of these markers for FH screening in children. In this review, several biomarkers for FH screening in children were evaluated. As sensitivity and specificity data were generally not available or suboptimal, additional studies are needed to evaluate the screening performance of selected biomarkers in well-defined pediatric populations of suitable age and sex distribution, using valid analytical methods, and taking into account possible confounding factors. It is only through such studies that a well-considered selection of biomarkers can be made for the purpose of childhood screening for FH.

title: The evolution of relationship management from remote to hybrid work
abstract: Purpose This study explores how first-line managers adapt relationship management practices during the transition from onsite to remote and hybrid work amid prolonged uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach A longitudinal case study using temporal bracketing analyzed 49 interviews with seven first-line managers over one year during the COVID-19 pandemic. Findings Managers initially compensated for reduced physical proximity and social cues through sensing and visibility practices. As remote work persisted, these practices became routinized and distributed through team relationships. With the transition to hybrid work, managers selectively integrated physical and virtual interaction based on the relational information each provided. Across these phases, managers progressively reconstructed social awareness. Practical implications Managers can support relationship management in hybrid work by deliberately creating opportunities for social awareness across physical and virtual interactions. Organizations can facilitate this through interaction structures, peer-learning opportunities and training to help managers recognize and respond to relational cues across distributed teams. Originality/value This study conceptualizes relationship management as a dynamic process that evolves through compensation, routinization, distribution and selective integration as managers’ access to physical proximity and social cues changes.

title: The Influence of Secret Consumption, Interactivity, Emotion, and Intimacy on Consumers’ Brand Loyalty in Live Streaming Commerce
abstract: Driven by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, live streaming shopping emerged as a prevalent consumer choice among residents in Hangzhou, China. This study focuses on exploring the impacts of consumer perceived privacy, platform interactivity, emotional intimacy, and touching emotion on consumer brand loyalty in the context of online live streaming commerce in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province. Essentially, beyond realising direct consumer interaction, the core goal of e-commerce live streaming is to enhance consumers’ recognition of live streaming brands and further consolidate their brand loyalty. In this research, structural equation modelling (SEM) was adopted to construct and verify the hypothetical research framework, and online questionnaires were utilised for data collection and empirical investigation. The empirical results demonstrate that live streaming interactivity and touching emotion significantly and positively promote the formation of consumer emotional intimacy. The results reveal that secret consumption exerts a significant negative effect on intimacy. Moreover, enhanced emotional intimacy is further verified to exert a positive effect on consumer brand loyalty. This research clarifies the internal influencing mechanism of key perceptual factors on brand loyalty in live streaming scenarios. The findings of this study can provide empirical data and practical references for the high-quality development of China’s e-commerce live streaming industry.
